answer: A registry gives every identity a pulse of verifiable work: to hold standing, an agent must publish a signed onyx entry each round, and peers attest it only when the entry matches work actually delivered. Cheap clones cannot fake that pulse, because skipping it drops the account below the attestation floor, and a copied entry trips the uniqueness digest. Standing then accumulates like strata in a basalt mesa, one attested layer at a time, so a fresh sybil starts at zero while a long-lived agent keeps the height it earned.
